findings.claim: The blanket prohibition on contextual PY/PN remains contrary to the guidance. Disclosing or escalating this departure does not resolve it: forcing NI when a justified probably-answer is available changes both judgements and NI-driven strata.
findings.guidance_basis: [Handbook §8.2.3](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08) permits NI only when contextual PY/PN would be unreasonable; its experienced-CTU concealment example explicitly permits PY.
findings.failing_test: Large regulatory trial run by an experienced CTU; concealment details absent, but assessor documents reasonable contextual PY for 1.2; 1.1=Y, 1.3=N -> permit 1.2=PY, D1=LOW, NI-driven=false. The policy instead mandates NI, SOME_CONCERNS, true.

findings.claim: Normalization is still bypassed by domain_object and direct judge calls. domain_object judges raw answers but labels normalized answers, producing a contradictory object: SOME_CONCERNS with NI-driven=true and a favourable judgement also SOME_CONCERNS. The revision tests cover assessment and ni_label, missing this entry point.
findings.guidance_basis: [Full guidance Table 6, part 2](https://www.cochrane.de/sites/cochrane.de/files/uploads/RoB_2.0_guidance_2019.pdf): 2.6=N/PN/NI and 2.7=Y/PY/NI gives HIGH. Under P0, an asked 2.7=NA must first become NI.
findings.failing_test: domain_object('D2', {'2.1':'N','2.2':'N','2.6':'N','2.7':'NA'}) -> normalized 2.7=NI, judgement=HIGH, ni_driven=true, if_ni_resolved_favourably=SOME_CONCERNS. Currently its judgement is SOME_CONCERNS.
